title: Multi-cloud data architecture
purpose: Four-region comparison of external cloud sources, deliberate shortcut, mirroring and copy paths, governed OneLake landing, and consumer-facing freshness and security trade-offs.
accessibleSummary: Multi-cloud data architecture. Cloud source systems; Virtualize, mirror, or copy; Governed OneLake products; Serve and operate across clouds.
longDescription: Four-region comparison of external cloud sources, deliberate shortcut, mirroring and copy paths, governed OneLake landing, and consumer-facing freshness and security trade-offs.

nodes.label: Cloud source systems
nodes.summary: S3, GCS, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, SaaS, and operational stores retain their own security and change models.
nodes.detail: Source location, ownership, egress, network and freshness requirements constrain integration.
nodes.whyItMatters: A modern pattern starts with source reality rather than a preferred Fabric tool.

evidence.note: Fabric supports connectors and patterns across Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and Salesforce.

drill.example: BigQuery facts and S3 Parquet must serve one Fabric product.
failureModes: Cross-cloud egress is ignored during design.

nodes.label: Virtualize, mirror, or copy
nodes.summary: Shortcuts avoid copies, mirroring replicates supported change feeds, and Data Factory materializes controlled batches.
nodes.detail: Choose the path per source and consumer rather than applying one mode to the whole estate.
nodes.whyItMatters: The three paths encode different ownership, freshness and failure semantics.

evidence.note: Guidance distinguishes shortcuts for zero-copy access, mirroring for replicated changes, and Copy jobs for batch movement.
Shortcuts reference supported external storage without moving the data.

drill.example: S3 is shortcut-mounted, Snowflake is mirrored, and Salesforce is copied nightly.
failureModes: A shortcut is chosen where source availability cannot meet BI SLA.

nodes.label: Governed OneLake products
nodes.summary: Paths appear in Fabric workspaces as governed, discoverable data products with lineage and security.
nodes.detail: The domain publishes stable contracts while retaining the source/path distinction in metadata.
nodes.whyItMatters: Governance convergence must not erase operational ownership.

evidence.note: OneLake provides the tenant-wide logical storage namespace.
OneLake security controls access to governed data paths.

processing: Apply ownership, labels, access and lineage
drill.example: Customer data records lineage to BigQuery, S3 and Salesforce.
failureModes: Delegated shortcut access is configured more broadly than intended.

nodes.label: Serve and operate across clouds
nodes.summary: BI, engineering and AI consumers use published products while telemetry tracks freshness, cost, failures and authorization.
nodes.detail: Operations reconcile source state with shortcut availability, mirror lag, and copy run status.
nodes.whyItMatters: Without path-specific SLOs, one polished catalog hides three different failure modes.

evidence.note: Fabric can track lineage from external sources through downstream consumers and orchestrate cross-cloud workflows.

drill.example: A dashboard exposes mirror freshness separately from nightly Salesforce load time.
failureModes: Consumers assume all datasets are equally current.
